rituals.name: THE BLAME PIE
rituals.title: THE BLAME PIE
rituals.goal: Own your real share of a problem without carrying everyone else's; sequence shared priorities.
rituals.steps:
1. Imagine a pie that stands for everything that caused the situation.
2. In your mind, give slices to your choices, other people, circumstances, systems, timing, and chance.
3. Make sure all slices together equal 100.
4. Focus only on your true share.
5. Picture one repair for your slice. Let the rest stay outside your responsibility.
rituals.winReward: Responsibility shrank to your actual slice, and one repair matched only what belonged to you.
rituals.win: Responsibility shrank to your actual slice, and one repair matched only what belonged to you.
supportsArray: Separate guilt from responsibility; name outside factors.
Make repair smaller than self-punishment; describe the behaviour, not yourself.
Do not punish yourself for learning; name the mistake.
Use equal standards; name the exact mistake.
Avoid global words like always; name the behaviour.
rituals.mindBend: Personalising turns influence into total causation; sharing the pie restores causes that guilt had erased.
rituals.formulaFlow: Imagine Pie → Share Slices → Check Whole → Find Slice → Choose Repair
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Set it down if sharing turns into punishment or erases genuine accountability.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.name: THE LIFE DIRECTION TEST
rituals.title: THE LIFE DIRECTION TEST
rituals.goal: Choose the next hour by direction, not by the loudest thought — calibrate shared timing.
rituals.steps:
1. Picture two arrows.
2. One arrow shows the next hour if you obey the thought. The other shows the hour if you follow a chosen value.
3. Name the likely behaviour at each arrow’s end.
4. Select by direction, not by mental volume.
rituals.winReward: You could see which option moved toward a value even while uncertainty stayed present.
rituals.win: You could see which option moved toward a value even while uncertainty stayed present.
supportsArray: Check whose goal; use values to choose trade-offs.
Make the next hour reflect it; protect important time.
Act before motivation; choose aligned action.
Use one priority; do not wait for motivation.
Review what the action costs; name today's value.
rituals.mindBend: A thought can be louder than a value and still be a worse compass.
rituals.formulaFlow: Picture → Make Room → Name Likely → Select Direction

rituals.name: CLOSE ONE DOOR FOR THIRTY SECONDS
rituals.title: CLOSE ONE DOOR FOR THIRTY SECONDS
rituals.ritual_name: CLOSE ONE DOOR FOR THIRTY SECONDS
rituals.goal: Resync right timing: test each leading option briefly to learn from your reaction without committing.
rituals.steps:
1. Picture the two leading options. Mentally fade one for thirty seconds and pretend it is unavailable; do not commit.
2. Notice the first specific reaction—relief, disappointment, bargaining, urgency, or no change. Name it in four words or fewer.
3. Bring that option back. Repeat once with the other option faded so both reactions receive the same test.
4. Use the clearer reaction as one piece of data, then choose only the next responsible move.
rituals.winReward: Each option was removed and restored once, giving you new data for the next responsible move.
rituals.win: Each option was removed and restored once, giving you new data for the next responsible move.
supportsArray: Name the non-negotiables; limit the options.
Reduce the options; ignore imagined regret.
Use strongest evidence; commit once chosen.
Stop researching after enough evidence; set a decision deadline.
Accept one trade-off; choose by the strongest evidence.
rituals.mindBend: Relief or disappointment after a temporary loss can reveal preference without pretending emotion is a final verdict.
rituals.formulaFlow: Close Door → Read Protest → Reopen Choice → Choose Next

PAUSE

rituals.name: VALUE BEFORE CERTAINTY
rituals.title: VALUE BEFORE CERTAINTY
rituals.goal: Let a chosen quality guide the next move before certainty arrives — order clean sequence.
rituals.steps:
1. Ask, “What quality should the next action carry?” Choose honesty, courage, care, fairness, or patience.
2. Define one visible movement that expresses that quality today.
3. Let certainty remain absent while the chosen quality gives direction.
rituals.winReward: One visible action expressed the value you picked even though doubt was still present.
rituals.win: One visible action expressed the value you picked even though doubt was still present.
supportsArray: Accept the trade-off; make the next hour reflect it.
Remove one conflicting commitment; name what matters today.
Keep meaning practical; pick one value for this decision.
Check whose goal; protect important time.
Choose aligned action; check whose goal you are chasing.
rituals.mindBend: Values answer how you want to move when certainty cannot answer what will happen.
rituals.formulaFlow: Ask Quality → Make Visible → Let Certainty

PAUSE

rituals.name: THE CONTROL GRAVEYARD
rituals.title: THE CONTROL GRAVEYARD
rituals.goal: Notice which control habits charge more over time than they repay now; order next steps.
rituals.steps:
1. Name everything used to control the feeling: checking, avoiding, numbing, arguing, extra certainty, overworking.
2. Beside each, picture the short-term payoff and the six-month bill.
3. Focus on any method whose bill exceeds its relief.
4. Choose one experiment in not paying that cost today.
rituals.winReward: You identified one short-term relief strategy whose longer bill was too high and skipped it once.
rituals.win: You identified one short-term relief strategy whose longer bill was too high and skipped it once.
supportsArray: Stop reopening choices; set a limit on checking.
Name what is known; delay reassurance seeking.
Accept small risk; notice when checking stops helping.
Choose good enough; ask what is controllable now.
Avoid reopening settled choices; choose a good-enough option.
rituals.mindBend: A coping move can work in the next minute and still make the next six months harder.
rituals.formulaFlow: Use Control → Picture Short → Focus Costs → Choose Experiment

PAUSE

This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.name: MORE THAN THIS STATE
rituals.title: MORE THAN THIS STATE
rituals.goal: Put the current painful state back inside a larger picture of you — calibrate shared sequence.
rituals.steps:
1. Name three roles you carry, two qualities others have witnessed, and one state present today.
2. Imagine a large circle around all six.
3. Place the current painful content inside the circle, not across the whole of you.
4. Ask which part of the larger picture should lead one simple action.
rituals.winReward: The painful state became one part of the circle, and another part could lead the next action.
rituals.win: The painful state became one part of the circle, and another part could lead the next action.
supportsArray: Decide your limit before answering; take time before saying yes.
State consequences clearly; repeat the same wording calmly.
Offer alternatives only if genuine; use a short no.
Offer only genuine options; do not overexplain the limit.
Keep the limit simple; notice resentment early.
rituals.mindBend: A state can occupy your attention without occupying your entire identity.
rituals.formulaFlow: Carry Qualities → Imagine Large → Place Painful → Ask Part

display.goal: Put the current painful state back inside a larger picture of you — calibrate shared sequence.

rituals.name: WHAT JOB IS THIS FEELING DOING?
rituals.title: WHAT JOB IS THIS FEELING DOING?
rituals.ritual_name: WHAT JOB IS THIS FEELING DOING?
rituals.goal: Learn what the feeling is trying to signal, prepare, or communicate before acting on it — align current pace.
rituals.steps:

2. What action is it preparing.
3. What is it communicating to others.
4. Keep answers concrete.
5. Use the information. Keep the behaviour under your supervision.

rituals.name: CHECK THE BODY VOLUME KNOBS
rituals.title: CHECK THE BODY VOLUME KNOBS
rituals.goal: Check basic body factors before treating the whole reaction as proof that something is wrong; sequence shared inputs.
rituals.steps:
1. Check five body factors: illness or pain, food or water, substances or withdrawal, sleep, and too much or too little movement.
2. Find the strongest factor you can safely change.
3. Make one helpful adjustment before deciding what the whole reaction means.
rituals.winReward: One changeable body factor was noticed and supported before you interpreted the reaction further.

rituals.name: PRELIVE THE HARD MOMENT
rituals.title: PRELIVE THE HARD MOMENT
rituals.goal: Balance current inputs: rehearse the hard moment with a realistic obstacle and a recovery plan.
rituals.steps:
1. Picture the trigger beginning.
2. Insert the exact skill you will use, the obstacle most likely to interrupt it, and your recovery if that obstacle wins once.
3. Continue the scene through a realistic ending—not a perfect one.
4. Then place one physical reminder where the event starts.
rituals.winReward: Your mental run included a mistake, a recovery, and a believable ending rather than perfection.
rituals.win: Your mental run included a mistake, a recovery, and a believable ending rather than perfection.
supportsArray: Compare against the brief; separate important errors from polish.

Ask what is actually required; ship useful work.
Make rough version; set finish time.
rituals.mindBend: Preparation becomes stronger when it rehearses how to continue after a wobble, not how to avoid every wobble.
rituals.formulaFlow: Picture → Use Obstacle → Continue Scene → Place Physical

rituals.name: FEELING OR FIXING?
rituals.title: FEELING OR FIXING?
rituals.goal: Decide whether the remaining problem needs calming, action, or support; sequence shared steps.
rituals.steps:
1. After body alarm drops, define the obstacle without emotional adjectives.
2. Ask if one specific action could change it.
3. If yes, choose and schedule that action.
4. If no, return to acceptance or support.
5. Do not keep using soothing when the door requires a key.
rituals.winReward: After the body settled, you could tell whether there was a practical door that needed a key.
rituals.win: After the body settled, you could tell whether there was a practical door that needed a key.
supportsArray: Avoid symptom searching; look at ordinary objects nearby.
Unclench your jaw; let breaths happen.
Use ordinary surroundings; let breathing stay natural.
Stay somewhere physically safe; stop body scanning.
Reduce caffeine; keep your body supported.
rituals.mindBend: Calming the body can lower the alarm, but it cannot solve a problem whose next step is a practical action.
rituals.formulaFlow: Drop Define → Ask Whether → Choose Action → Return Acceptance → Stop Soothing

rituals.name: FINISH THE LOOK
rituals.title: FINISH THE LOOK
rituals.goal: Let your eyes finish checking the present before deciding where attention belongs; order current inputs.
rituals.steps:
1. Let your eyes move before your head.
2. Slowly scan left, centre, right, behind if safe, and toward an exit.
3. Name present cues of choice, support, and distance from threat.
4. Allow the neck to follow only within comfort.
5. End by selecting where attention belongs now.
rituals.winReward: Choice, support, distance, and an exit were all visually located without forcing the neck or returning to the past.

rituals.name: LET BREATH BREATHE YOU
rituals.title: LET BREATH BREATHE YOU
rituals.goal: Let breathing happen by itself while you simply notice its movement; coordinate working inputs.
rituals.steps:
1. Follow three natural breaths exactly as they occur.
2. Do not deepen, slow, count, or improve them.
3. Notice where each begins by itself and where it ends without instruction.
4. Between breaths, let the body choose again.
5. Your only action is witnessing what already knows how to move.
rituals.winReward: Three breaths began and ended without being corrected, deepened, slowed, or counted.
rituals.win: Three breaths began and ended without being corrected, deepened, slowed, or counted.
supportsArray: Reduce commentary; return to the room.
Use fewer words; notice where attention goes.
Drop the need to solve it; notice the thought.
Do not debate every detail; avoid building a larger story.
Use simple present-tense facts; notice the thought, then step back.
rituals.mindBend: Breathing can reveal how much control is optional: the body keeps producing the next breath before you issue an instruction.
rituals.formulaFlow: Follow Breaths → Leave Alone → Start → Let Body → Witness Motion

rituals.goal: Settle into an easy breathing rhythm before changing depth or volume — tune clean signals.

4. Drop the counting and allow one natural breath.

rituals.steps:

rituals.name: WHAT SURVIVES THREE STATES?
rituals.title: WHAT SURVIVES THREE STATES?
rituals.goal: Balance shared choices: test which identity claims still make sense across waking, dreaming, and deep sleep.
rituals.steps:
1. Picture what appears in waking, what appears in dreams, and what is absent or inferred in deep sleep.
2. Ask which claims of identity remain supported across all three.
3. Hold conclusions lightly; this is an inquiry into ongoing sense, not a demand for belief.
rituals.winReward: The inquiry held several states in view without forcing a final belief about what you are.
rituals.win: The inquiry held several states in view without forcing a final belief about what you are.
supportsArray: Do one action for your life; choose your own measure.
Use your own timeline; notice what you cannot see.
Compare with your past self; name one thing already working.
Stop checking their numbers; check your own progress.
Use your own priorities; limit social media exposure.
rituals.mindBend: An identity can feel permanent while depending heavily on the state in which it is being examined.
rituals.formulaFlow: Picture Appears → Ask Claims → Hold Conclusions
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Discontinue if sleep-related inquiry worsens insomnia or unreality.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.name: SAME VALUE, TWO OUTCOMES
rituals.title: SAME VALUE, TWO OUTCOMES
rituals.goal: Keep the same value steady across both success and failure; check usable sequence.
rituals.steps:
1. Imagine the action succeeding.
2. State what that value asks of you next.
3. Imagine it failing.
4. State how the same value responds there.
5. Let outcome alter strategy, not your ethical centre.
rituals.winReward: The imagined outcome changed strategy, but the value still supplied a next action in either direction.
rituals.win: The imagined outcome changed strategy, but the value still supplied a next action in either direction.
supportsArray: Notice absolute words like always; test the assumption.
Ask what would change your mind; separate possibility from probability.
Check the base rate; look for one missing fact.
Check what you actually know; question absolute words.
Delay the verdict; ask what else could fit.
rituals.mindBend: Results should update tactics, not automatically rewrite the principle that made the action worth taking.
rituals.formulaFlow: Imagine Action → State Governing → Imagine Failing → State Value → Let Outcome
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Do not use equanimity to ignore grief, accountability, or material consequences.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.name: THE SUSTAINABLE MIDDLE
rituals.title: THE SUSTAINABLE MIDDLE
rituals.goal: Move one swinging habit into a middle range you could repeat for two weeks — set current rhythm.
rituals.steps:
1. Review sleep, food, effort, practice, and rest.
2. Find the area swinging between too much and too little.
3. Set a middle range you could repeat for two weeks.
4. Use the smallest adjustment that moves into that band today.
rituals.winReward: Sleep, food, effort, practice, or rest shifted toward a sustainable band instead of another extreme.
rituals.win: Sleep, food, effort, practice, or rest shifted toward a sustainable band instead of another extreme.
supportsArray: Check what you actually know; ask what would disprove it.
Separate guess from evidence; delay the verdict.
Delay major conclusions when upset; check the base rate.
Check the whole situation; use current facts.
Avoid treating guesses as facts; check another angle.
rituals.mindBend: Extremes can feel committed because they are intense. Repeatability is a better test of whether a routine can actually carry you.
rituals.formulaFlow: Rest Review → Find Area → Set Middle → Choose Smallest

rituals.name: EMPTY THE MENTAL COUNTERTOP
rituals.title: EMPTY THE MENTAL COUNTERTOP
rituals.goal: Empty every loose obligation into one trusted place before deciding what comes first — sequence real choices.
rituals.steps:
1. Catch every task, question, promise, and loose obligation into one trusted place.
2. Do not organise while emptying.
3. When the mind offers silence, sort entries into do, schedule, delegate, reference, or delete.
4. Choose only the first physical action.
rituals.winReward: The mental pile reached silence, then each item received a home and only one physical action remained active.
rituals.win: The mental pile reached silence, then each item received a home and only one physical action remained active.

Take a short break; park secondary tasks.
Clear visual clutter; finish or park one open loop.
Return after interruptions; put the phone out of reach.
Return to one target; close what you do not need.
rituals.mindBend: Working memory keeps unfinished items loud when it fears they will be lost. Capture can quiet them before solving anything.
rituals.formulaFlow: Question Promise → Empty First → Sort Entries → Choose Physical

rituals.title: BRAID THE SIGNALS
rituals.goal: Let two competing signals share attention before deciding which one matters — check working sequence.
rituals.steps:
1. Choose the two signals fighting for attention.
2. Alternate A–B–A–B at a slow fixed rhythm.
3. Then hold both at the same time for one interval, noticing difference without choosing.
4. Decide only after the braid is complete.
rituals.winReward: A–B alternation became simultaneous awareness, and the decision waited until both signals had been fully represented.

Choose one target; take a real screen break.

rituals.name: MATCH THE PRESSURE, THEN ZERO IT
rituals.title: MATCH THE PRESSURE, THEN ZERO IT
rituals.ritual_name: MATCH THE PRESSURE, THEN ZERO IT
rituals.goal: Balance real choices: match two sides of physical pressure, then lower both together back to zero.
rituals.steps:
1. Press palms together—or both hands into one cushion—at about twenty percent effort. Keep breathing ordinary.
2. Adjust until neither side wins and the pressure feels equal. Hold that match for two seconds.
3. Lower both sides together through three gentle levels: fifteen, ten, then five percent.
4. Reach zero, rest both hands on a stable surface, and observe whether the urge to press returns.
rituals.winReward: Equal resistance stepped down through lighter levels until your hands rested and the urge to press could be checked.
rituals.win: Equal resistance stepped down through lighter levels until your hands rested and the urge to press could be checked.
supportsArray: Keep your hands busy; drink some water.
Remember urges peak and fall; avoid bargaining with the urge.
Ride the peak; use your hands.
Make access less convenient; move away from the cue.
Delay acting for ten minutes; make access harder.
rituals.mindBend: The body can learn release through symmetry. Lowering matched pressure together shows that stopping does not require one side to lose.
rituals.formulaFlow: Press Equal → Match Force → Step Down → Reach Zero
rituals.safety:
PAUSE

rituals.name: SEPARATE THE MENTAL INBOXES
rituals.title: SEPARATE THE MENTAL INBOXES
rituals.goal: Sort mental items by type before deciding what deserves attention first; balance clear priorities.
rituals.steps:
1. Put each mental item into IDEA, OBLIGATION, FEAR, MEMORY, or QUESTION.
2. Give each category its own way of being handled.
3. Choose priority only after sorting, so intensity does not decide the order.
rituals.winReward: Ideas, obligations, fears, memories, and questions were separated before priority was chosen.
rituals.win: Ideas, obligations, fears, memories, and questions were separated before priority was chosen.
supportsArray: Keep one task visible; finish or park one open loop.
Close extra tabs; return after interruptions.
Take a short break; mute alerts.
Take a real screen break; silence nonessential notifications.
Clear visual clutter; use one screen.
rituals.mindBend: When everything shares one mental inbox, the loudest item jumps the queue. Sorting first gives priority a fairer chance.
rituals.formulaFlow: Question Capture → Give Category → Don't Determine
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Add categories sparingly; excessive sorting can become avoidance.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: WANT NOW / PROTECT LATER
rituals.goal: Coordinate shared signals: acknowledge what the urge wants now while protecting what future life still needs.
rituals.steps:
1. Picture what the present urge wants, then what future life is worth protecting.
2. Name the cost each imposes on the other.
3. Choose one action that acknowledges desire while keeping the valued asset intact.
rituals.winReward: The chosen move made room for desire without sacrificing the longer-term asset you named.
rituals.win: The chosen move made room for desire without sacrificing the longer-term asset you named.
supportsArray: Leave the trigger; remember urges peak and fall.
Ride the peak; change rooms if possible.
Keep your hands busy; eat or drink if hunger matters.
Drink some water; use your hands.
Delay ten minutes; make access harder.
rituals.mindBend: An urge speaks from a short time horizon. Adding future cost does not erase desire, but it changes who gets represented in the decision.

rituals.name: THE BORING DOSE
rituals.title: THE BORING DOSE
rituals.goal: Practise a small, fixed dose of boredom without adding stimulation or extending the challenge — sequence mixed signals.
rituals.steps:
1. Choose a safe boring task and decide on ten slow breaths.
2. Decide that no extra stimulation will be added during those breaths.
3. Notice boredom’s body sensations until the tenth breath.
4. Stop there, even if you could continue; increase future doses slowly.
rituals.winReward: Ten slow breaths passed with the boring task unchanged, and the exercise stopped exactly at the planned dose.
rituals.win: Ten slow breaths passed with the boring task unchanged, and the exercise stopped exactly at the planned dose.
supportsArray: Use ordinary surroundings; unclench your jaw and shoulders.
Wait out the surge; keep movements gentle.
Stay somewhere physically safe; reduce caffeine.
Let breathing stay natural; look at ordinary objects nearby.
Reduce extra stimulation; loosen your shoulders.
rituals.mindBend: Boredom becomes more commanding when every trace is immediately fed stimulation. A measured dose teaches that under-stimulation has an end.
rituals.formulaFlow: Choose Boring → Remove Extras → Stay → End Cleanly
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Adapt for attention disorders and never use boredom as punishment.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.goal: Stop when your thinking quality clearly drops and keep the last conclusion you could still trust — set steady rhythm.
rituals.steps:

rituals.name: THE TURNING POINT AT HALF SPEED
rituals.title: THE TURNING POINT AT HALF SPEED
rituals.ritual_name: THE TURNING POINT AT HALF SPEED
rituals.goal: Review only the turning point slowly enough to keep observation separate from motive; order right sequence.
rituals.steps:
1. Choose no more than ten seconds of the interaction, beginning before the moment that felt different.
2. Run those ten seconds once in imagination at half speed. Keep only what you can actually observe: words, pauses, volume, face, and movement.
3. Stop at the first change and name it without motive: ‘the pause lengthened,’ ‘the volume rose,’ or ‘the reply shortened.’
4. Keep that one fact. End the review before building another explanation.
rituals.winReward: One visible change—pause, volume, face, movement, or reply length—was kept while the review ended before explanation multiplied.

rituals.goal: Make active concerns compete for one attention block using consequence and reversibility, not noise — coordinate mixed inputs.
rituals.steps:
1. Let each active concern bid on urgency, consequence, reversibility, and information value.
2. Total the four ratings.
3. Award one protected block to the highest bidder and deny all others entry until time expires.
4. Re-auction with updated evidence.
rituals.winReward: Urgency, consequence, reversibility, and information value awarded the next block to one concern while the others waited.
rituals.win: Urgency, consequence, reversibility, and information value awarded the next block to one concern while the others waited.
supportsArray: Choose by the strongest evidence; ignore imagined regret.
Commit once chosen; name must-haves.
Ask what failure would cost; reduce the options.
Set a deadline; choose the option you can support.
Accept one trade-off; stop researching after enough evidence.
rituals.mindBend: Attention is scarce enough to require allocation. Allowing every concern partial access can leave none with enough time to become useful.
rituals.formulaFlow: Let Active → Total → Protect Block → Update Evidence
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Emergency signals may override the auction immediately.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.name: TURN THE LOOP INTO FIVE ICONS
rituals.title: TURN THE LOOP INTO FIVE ICONS
rituals.ritual_name: TURN THE LOOP INTO FIVE ICONS
rituals.goal: Tune shared inputs; turn a repetitive thought loop into simple images and interrupt the first repeated meaning.
rituals.steps:
1. Imagine five boxes. Do not use full sentences.
2. Give each of the last five thought turns one simple inner picture.
3. Notice the first picture whose meaning comes back later.
4. At the next box, picture one real fact to check or one small action to take, then stop imagining.
rituals.winReward: The first returning icon exposed the loop, then one real fact or action replaced another thought turn.
rituals.win: The first returning icon exposed the loop, then one real fact or action replaced another thought turn.
supportsArray: Name one useful action; use your hands.
Stop solving the unsolvable; do something that needs your hands.
Shift attention outward; set a clear stopping point.
Ask if any new information exists; name one action.
Limit how long you review it; end the replay.
rituals.mindBend: Loops can feel complex because the sentences change; reducing them to icons reveals when the same meaning is simply wearing new wording.
rituals.formulaFlow: No Sentences → Imagine Signs → Spot Return → Choose Exit
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Do not imagine this while driving; stop if the mental sequence becomes compulsive, perfectionistic, or more distressing than the thought.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.name: SCULPT THE PROBLEM
rituals.title: SCULPT THE PROBLEM
rituals.goal: Move one imagined part of a problem and translate that spatial shift into a real action — order usable sequence.
rituals.steps:
1. Picture the problem as positions for people, obstacles, resources, and goals.
2. Place those positions as they feel now.
3. Move only one position or distance toward a more workable configuration.
4. Name the real-life action that matches that imagined shift.
rituals.winReward: A person, obstacle, resource, or goal changed position and produced one concrete move in the actual situation.
rituals.win: A person, obstacle, resource, or goal changed position and produced one concrete move in the actual situation.
supportsArray: Open the task; start with one minute.
Enter through easy work; use a visible cue.
Choose a rough beginning; prepare first.
Do the easiest useful part; make the first move tiny.
Begin while unsure; lower the quality bar.
rituals.mindBend: Spatial imagination can reveal leverage that verbal analysis misses because distance and position make relationships between parts visible.
rituals.formulaFlow: Imagine Map → Arrange → Shift One → Translate
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Do not treat symbolic placement as factual evidence about other people.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.name: REMEMBER THE FUTURE IN ADVANCE
rituals.title: REMEMBER THE FUTURE IN ADVANCE
rituals.goal: Imagine the scene just after completion, then trace backward to the first movement you can do now; resync clean timing.
rituals.steps:
1. Create a memory-like scene set just after completing the action.
2. Include time, location, body posture, one sensory cue, along with what you did when difficulty appeared.
3. Look backward from that imagined completion to the first real movement and do it now.
rituals.winReward: A future memory supplied posture, sensory detail, and a coping response that led directly back to a real first action.
rituals.win: A future memory supplied posture, sensory detail, and a coping response that led directly back to a real first action.
supportsArray: Feel your feet; return to one real sound.
Slow your physical pace; keep eyes open.
Keep your eyes on something steady; hear one real sound.
Notice three colours; look around the room.
Notice room temperature; feel both feet.
rituals.mindBend: Planning backward from a completed scene can make the starting step clearer than trying to push forward from uncertainty.
rituals.formulaFlow: Create Memory → Include Time → Look Backward
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Keep future scenes realistic rather than using fantasy as avoidance.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.name: INTERVIEW THE OBSTACLE
rituals.title: INTERVIEW THE OBSTACLE
rituals.goal: Calibrate shared choices: ask the obstacle what it is protecting and negotiate one step that respects the valid need.
rituals.steps:
1. Give the obstacle a character and ask three questions: What are you protecting.
2. What do you fear will happen.
3. What would make one step acceptable.
4. Picture its answers, then negotiate a small action that protects the valid need without handing over total control.
rituals.winReward: Fear, protection, and conditions for movement became explicit enough to make a small agreement possible.
rituals.win: Fear, protection, and conditions for movement became explicit enough to make a small agreement possible.
supportsArray: Start smaller; make it visible.
Do the easiest useful part; set a two-minute timer.
Choose tiny action; prepare first.
Open only what you need; start with one minute.
Touch the first item; open the task.
rituals.mindBend: Resistance often looks irrational from outside its job. Once its protective function is named, the negotiation changes.
rituals.formulaFlow: Give Obstacle → Ask Fear → Make Step → Picture Negotiate
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Do not personify intrusive voices or experiences if that worsens symptoms.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.name: IMAGINE THE INNER MACHINE
rituals.title: IMAGINE THE INNER MACHINE
rituals.goal: Map the full trigger-to-result loop and change one link instead of fighting the whole system — match moving parts.
rituals.steps:
1. Imagine the trigger, meaning, physical feeling, urge, action, result, and feedback.
2. Imagine how each part affects the next and where the loop returns.
3. Notice one place where a small change may shift the whole loop.
4. Try that small change once.
rituals.winReward: A single point in the sequence shifted once, creating fresh evidence about how the larger pattern responds.
rituals.win: A single point in the sequence shifted once, creating fresh evidence about how the larger pattern responds.
supportsArray: Eat if hungry; move away from the cue.
Avoid bargaining with the urge; tell someone early.
Make access less convenient; drink some water.
Eat or drink if hunger matters; delay ten minutes.
Do one incompatible activity; keep your hands busy.
rituals.mindBend: Complex habits can feel indivisible until one link changes; a loop only needs one altered connection to stop being exactly the same loop.
rituals.formulaFlow: Imagine Parts → See Links → Find Lever → Test It
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Keep the mental picture simple. Stop if you begin analysing without taking action.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.name: BORROW ONE MOVE FROM THE AVATAR
rituals.title: BORROW ONE MOVE FROM THE AVATAR
rituals.ritual_name: BORROW ONE MOVE FROM THE AVATAR
rituals.goal: Borrow one useful behaviour from an imagined capable figure without trying to become them — tune mixed signals.

rituals.name: PUT TIME ARROWS ON THE OPTIONS
rituals.title: PUT TIME ARROWS ON THE OPTIONS
rituals.ritual_name: PUT TIME ARROWS ON THE OPTIONS
rituals.goal: Notice which options improve, decay, stay stable, or expire as time passes — order working inputs.
rituals.steps:

rituals.name: WHAT WOULD THIS FACT CHANGE?
rituals.title: WHAT WOULD THIS FACT CHANGE?
rituals.goal: Order shared sequence; collect only facts that could actually change what you decide.
rituals.steps:
1. For every desired data point, picture how a positive, negative, or neutral result would alter the decision.
2. If no result changes action, stop collecting it.
3. Prioritise the fact with the largest possible decision swing.
rituals.winReward: A desired data point stayed only if at least one possible result would change your action.
rituals.win: A desired data point stayed only if at least one possible result would change your action.
supportsArray: Use a visible cue; start before you feel ready.
Use two minutes; touch the first item.
Open only what you need; enter through easy work.
Remove one barrier; choose tiny action.
Remove one obvious distraction; cut the task.
rituals.mindBend: Information has decision value only when different answers lead somewhere different. Otherwise collection is movement without leverage.
rituals.formulaFlow: Point Positive → Stop Collecting → Test Relevance
rituals.safety:
PAUSE

This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.name: RUN A TWO-OPTION KNOCKOUT
rituals.title: RUN A TWO-OPTION KNOCKOUT
rituals.goal: Compare two options at a time using one declared criterion and let the survivor earn the next look; resync signals.
rituals.steps:
1. Picture the available options into a simple bracket. Give an unpaired option a bye rather than inventing a rival.
2. Choose one criterion that matters for this round and picture it above the bracket. Do not switch it mid-game.
3. Compare only two options at a time. Advance the one that better meets the declared criterion.
4. Crown the final survivor as the next option to inspect or act on—not as a permanent life verdict.
rituals.winReward: The bracket produced a next option to inspect without pretending the winner was a permanent life verdict.
rituals.win: The bracket produced a next option to inspect without pretending the winner was a permanent life verdict.
supportsArray: Notice the trigger; change the environment first.
Make the new habit easier; delay the routine.
Remove easy access; change one cue.
Change the environment; expect slips and restart quickly.
Move the cue; interrupt the sequence.
rituals.mindBend: Choice overload shrinks when comparisons are local; deciding between two things is cognitively different from holding the whole field at once.
rituals.formulaFlow: Seed Options → Pick Criterion → Play Pairs → Crown Next
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
For high-stakes choices, use the winner only as the next research step and include qualified advice and all safety criteria.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: THE PAST INVESTMENT GETS NO NEW VOTE
rituals.ritual_name: THE PAST INVESTMENT GETS NO NEW VOTE
rituals.goal: Ignore what is already spent and compare the choices only from today forward — resync current parts.
rituals.steps:

rituals.name: HIDE THE CROWD’S ANSWER
rituals.title: HIDE THE CROWD’S ANSWER
rituals.goal: Set shared timing: form your own quality judgment before looking at ratings, likes, rankings, or social consensus.
rituals.steps:

rituals.name: GIVE THE BELIEF A POSTCODE
rituals.title: GIVE THE BELIEF A POSTCODE
rituals.goal: Tune current rhythm; shrink a broad belief until it states where, when, and with whom it actually fits.
rituals.steps:
1. Say the belief silently.
2. Think about when, where, with whom, and under what conditions it may be true.
3. Picture one real case where it fits.
4. Picture one real case where the belief does not fit.
5. Say a smaller, more accurate version of the belief.
rituals.winReward: One fitting case and one exception produced a smaller statement that was more accurate than the original rule.
rituals.win: One fitting case and one exception produced a smaller statement that was more accurate than the original rule.
supportsArray: Repeat without arguing; keep the limit simple.
Take time before saying yes; repeat the same wording calmly.
Use a short no; keep consequences realistic.
State consequences clearly; delay your answer.
Offer only genuine options; use one clear sentence.
rituals.mindBend: A belief that works only under certain conditions is not a law; context turns absolutes back into local rules.
rituals.formulaFlow: Name Belief → Imagine Limits → Test Inside → Test Outside → Shrink Rule
rituals.safety:
PAUSE

rituals.name: CUT THE AFTER-SOCIAL LOOP
rituals.title: CUT THE AFTER-SOCIAL LOOP
rituals.goal: Coordinate timing: stop looping over an awkward moment by separating what happened from the extra meaning your mind is adding.
rituals.steps:
1. Say the exact words or action you keep running through your mind once, with no commentary.
2. Name one fact about how the other person actually responded. If you do not know, say “I don’t know.”
3. Name the harsh conclusion your mind added afterward.
4. Replace it with the smallest fairer conclusion that still fits the facts.
5. Return to one ordinary action in the present.
rituals.winReward: The awkward moment became an event you can learn from, not a verdict you have to keep reliving.
rituals.win: The awkward moment became an event you can learn from, not a verdict you have to keep reliving.

display.title: FACTS AFTER THE ARGUMENT
display.goal: Stop circling the past by keeping one fact and leaving the unanswered question alone — calibrate current priorities.
display.numberedSteps:
1. Name one plain reminder.
2. Set the remaining requests aside.
3. Name the question you are leaving alone.
display.win: The reminder stayed brief, extra requests were parked, and the old question did not receive another rehearsal.
display.mindBend: Circling the past cannot edit the event, but it can repeatedly alter your present state. Repetition and resolution are different processes.
display.formulaFlow: Catch Thought → Park Rest → Shut Door

rituals.name: REASSURANCE ENDS HERE
rituals.title: REASSURANCE ENDS HERE
rituals.goal: Sequence next steps: stop outsourcing certainty to reassurance and decide from the evidence you actually have.
rituals.steps:
1. Name the evidence that is actually missing.
2. Say the idea in one real-world sentence.
3. Review the fact once, choose the next move, and stop.
rituals.winReward: The missing evidence was named, the fact was reviewed once, and the next move happened without another reassurance round.
rituals.win: The missing evidence was named, the fact was reviewed once, and the next move happened without another reassurance round.
supportsArray: Use a deadline; name what is unknown.
Stop reopening choices; choose a good-enough option.
Leave one doubt; notice when checking stops helping.
Accept a small margin of risk; limit checking.
Set a limit on checking; delay reassurance.
rituals.mindBend: Reassurance can reduce discomfort without increasing evidence. When those are confused, relief starts masquerading as proof.
rituals.formulaFlow: Hold Question → Sample It → Review Once

rituals.name: THE NO-CHECK DECISION
rituals.title: THE NO-CHECK DECISION
rituals.goal: Make the needed decision through one chosen lens and stop checking whether the intrusive idea has disappeared; coordinate current steps.
rituals.steps:
1. Name the decision you actually need to make.
2. Pick one lens that counts for this round—safe, useful, kind, necessary, or time-bound.
3. Choose the option that best fits that lens.
4. Say, “Decision made for now.”
5. Continue for one minute without checking whether the idea is gone.
rituals.winReward: One criterion guided the choice, the decision was closed for now, and the next minute continued without intrusion monitoring.
rituals.win: One criterion guided the choice, the decision was closed for now, and the next minute continued without intrusion monitoring.
supportsArray: Return to the task; notice mental content.
Delay reassurance; reduce deliberate monitoring.
Do not neutralise; return to the current task.
Avoid confessing for relief; allow uncertainty.
Let thoughts pass; skip confession for relief.
rituals.mindBend: Checking whether an idea is gone makes absence a condition for progress. A decision can finish while mental noise remains.
rituals.formulaFlow: Name Decision → Pick Lens → Choose Fit → Close Choice → Skip Check
